instructions.task: This is a chat in a study. The persuader asks the persuadee to donate part of the persuadee's task payment (up to about $2) to a children's charity (Save the Children); the donation is taken from the payment after the chat. Judge where the persuadee ended up by the end of the chat: what did they finally commit to about donating from this task payment?
notes: Only the persuadee's decision counts, not the persuader's.
If the persuadee changes their mind, their final stance counts.

What matters most is whether the persuadee names how much they will give: a stated figure or share, however small, implausibly large, or promised for a later time, signals a donation; agreeing in principle without ever saying how much does not. The exception is a persuadee who says they will give through another channel instead (going to the charity's own website, donating there or in person on their own): that does not count, even with a figure.

Saying yes to a specific figure that the persuader proposed for the persuadee's own donation counts the same as the persuadee naming that figure. Saying yes to a general question such as whether they would like to donate does not settle an amount.
A figure offered only as a possibility (with may, might, maybe, perhaps, or I could possibly) and never firmed up is tentative, not a commitment.
Talk about the persuadee's past or usual giving to other causes is not a decision about this donation.

criteria.firm_amount: The persuadee commits to donating a specific amount or share (a number of cents or dollars, half, all of it) and does not take it back or move it to another channel.
criteria.accepts_proposed_amount: The persuader proposes a specific figure (a number of cents or dollars, or a share such as half) for the persuadee's own donation, and the persuadee accepts that figure (says yes, agrees, that works) without naming a different one or backing out.
criteria.vague_quantity: The persuadee commits to giving and describes the size only loosely, such as a small amount, a little, or some of the payment.
criteria.large_amount: The persuadee names a figure larger than the task payment could cover (such as tens, hundreds or more dollars) as their donation, showing willingness but a misunderstanding of the setup.
criteria.later_with_amount: The persuadee names a figure they will give at a later time (next week, when paid), without saying it will go through the charity's website or some other channel.
criteria.agrees_no_amount: The persuadee says yes to donating or that they will donate, but no amount is ever settled: they never say how much, even loosely (all, half, a little), and never accept a specific figure proposed for them; this includes saying yes only to a general request to donate.
criteria.tentative: The persuadee only says they might, may, or will consider donating, including floating a figure as a mere possibility (maybe a few cents, I may do a quarter) without ever firming it up.
criteria.other_channel: The persuadee says they will give through the charity's website or on their own outside this chat task, instead of through the task, whether or not they name a figure.
criteria.later_no_amount: The persuadee says they will donate at some later time or after doing research, without naming any figure.
criteria.other_help_only: The persuadee offers only other help, such as volunteering, spreading the word, or getting others to donate, but no money of their own.
criteria.refuses: The persuadee declines to donate, chooses zero, or decides to keep the whole payment, including retracting an earlier offer.
criteria.never_decided: The donation is never settled by the persuadee: the chat drifts to other topics or to their giving to other causes, the persuadee only asks questions, or the text is too garbled to show any decision.
